dek.en: A 2026 kickoff call, the plan for a global network of data accelerators anyone can run, a topology video series, and a coding workshop for researchers.

en: Optimum opened 2026 with a list: make Ethereum faster, raise validator yields, bring congestion to all time lows, and deploy a global set of Flexnodes to power it all. January was mostly about the last item.

Flexnodes are the part of Optimum the community can imagine running itself: light nodes on a laptop or phone that speed up data and get paid for it. Optimum was careful to say the rollout would be controlled at first, but the questions in the replies, who can join, from where, for what, showed how much interest there was.
Optimum held a 2026 kickoff call in the Discord on 16 January with testnet updates and the road to mainnet.
On 20 January it published Flexnodes: A Global Network of Data Accelerators, describing light nodes paid through a Latency Marketplace, with no regional restrictions planned.
A YouTube series explained network topologies, Kishori Konwar appeared as CTO, and Optimum announced DeCo, a workshop on decentralized coding at MIT for March.

title.en: A global network of data accelerators

body.en: On 20 January Optimum published its plan for Flexnodes, nodes that receive block data, cut it into coded pieces and send them on to validators, which decode once they have enough. Any internet connected device could become one by running Optimum’s software, the post said, though the first phase would be controlled, starting with existing validator partners. Operators would be paid through a Latency Marketplace in which validators pay for the coded pieces they need. Asked on 26 January, Optimum said no regional restrictions were planned.

sources: Optimum on X, no regional restrictions

body.en: On 6 January Optimum invited the Discord to its 2026 Kickoff Call on 16 January: the latest testnet updates, what was next on the road to mainnet and community plans. It framed the year in one line: 2026 is the year RLNC goes from testing to production. A day earlier it had told a member that mump2p was built for validators, and that Flexnodes would be where the wider community could take part.

sources: Optimum on X, testing to production

title.en: A video series on network shapes

body.en: Between 14 and 30 January Optimum published a Network Topology series on YouTube: how topology affects throughput, then point to point TCP, tree multicast, RLNC and finally Optimum’s Flexnodes, each in four to six minutes. On 29 January a 35 minute conversation followed in which Médard, CTO Kishori Konwar and senior researcher Nicolas Nicolaou took apart the blockchain trilemma. Optimum’s claim in the same weeks: consistent propagation of 150 to 400 ms across its test network.

title.en: DeCo, a workshop on decentralized coding

body.en: On 23 January Optimum called on researchers, protocol developers and technical leaders working where coding theory meets decentralized systems to join DeCo, the Decentralized Coding Workshop, held at MIT in March. It was the first event Optimum organised for academics rather than crypto audiences.

title.en: A first quarter on the road

body.en: On 27 January Optimum published where the team would be in the first quarter: CODED, a side event at Consensus Hong Kong co-hosted with AWS on 11 February, ETHDenver from 17 to 21 February with a Médard keynote, DeCo in March and EthCC in Cannes, where product lead Sajida Zouarhi would present research on the cost of tail latency in the transaction pipeline.

title.en: From the Discord: the ice hunt runs long

body.en: The third treasure hunt was extended to 19 January to give late hunters a second wind, with a new hint on the community call, and its winners were drawn live on the call of 29 January. Regional channels changed too: from 28 January members unlock their region by reacting with a flag in start-here. Questions for the 16 January kickoff call were collected in advance.
